title: Blended wing aircraft

core_architecture: lifting blended-wing body with laterally extending wings
one or more engines positioned at or near the aft body
fan located downstream of the combustion section in a pusher arrangement
fan inlet arranged to ingest body boundary-layer airflow
core turbomachine inlet may be routed separately from fan ingestion flow
body flowpath can include inlet channels that guide air toward the engine
surface shaping upstream of an inlet may condition incoming flow
variable-pitch fan architecture may support forward and reverse thrust modes
engine installation may be top-side, bottom-side, trailing-edge integrated, pylon-mounted, or overhung depending on the design variant
open-rotor and nacelle-enclosed fan variants are both contemplated
engineering_relevance: treat airframe and propulsion as one coupled aerodynamic system
use boundary-layer ingestion as a drag-reduction design variable rather than only an engine-placement choice
separate fan-flow management from core-engine inlet requirements when evaluating pusher configurations
compare integrated trailing-edge installation against pylon-mounted installation using structural, maintenance, acoustic, thermal, and distortion metrics
evaluate variable-pitch fan logic as part of propulsion-airframe integration instead of as an isolated engine feature
optimize around system-level efficiency, not only isolated fan or body efficiency

publicly_described_functional_concepts: aft pusher arrangement shortens the mechanical distance between drive turbine and fan
pusher fan can ingest boundary-layer flow from the aircraft body
re-energizing slower boundary-layer air can reduce aircraft-level drag
fan flow and turbomachine-core inlet flow can be managed through different pathways
flowpath channels and upstream shaping features can condition inlet flow
variable-pitch fan can provide both forward and reverse thrust modes
multiple laterally spaced engines can be integrated at the aft body
open-rotor and enclosed-fan architectures can be evaluated within the same propulsion-airframe concept family

claim_scope_signals.independent_claim_theme: blended-wing aircraft with a body-mounted aft propulsion arrangement in which a fan is downstream of the combustion section, including variants that integrate the engine with lower-body or trailing-edge flowpath features
claim_scope_signals.legal_scope_rule: The controlling claims, prosecution history, continuation/divisional lineage, legal status, territorial scope, and any later amendments must be checked in the official record before infringement, licensing, or freedom-to-operate conclusions.

design_divergence_defaults: start from independent mission, payload, range, noise, maintainability, and certification requirements rather than reproducing the disclosed geometry
use a parameterized digital twin instead of fixed patent dimensions
compare pusher, tractor, open-rotor, and distributed-electric alternatives before selecting a configuration
independently derive inlet shaping from CFD and distortion limits rather than copying figure geometry
treat top, bottom, trailing-edge, pylon, and overhung installations as a trade space
maintain provenance for every patent-derived architecture signal
require qualified aerospace review and applicable airworthiness processes before any physical flight article

mandatory_safety_boundaries: no claim that patent geometry is flight-ready
no flight-test release without qualified engineering review
independent propulsion and fire-safety analysis required
airworthiness and regulatory review required for physical aircraft
patent and licensing review required before commercial release
